title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{p1}
Let problem (1) be conditionally well-posed on a compact set $K, K \subset X$. Then a neural network can solve the problem with an accuracy no better than $\bar{\varepsilon}=\max \left\{\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon _{val}\right\}$.

body_md: An analogue of the concept of a regularized dataset was previously considered in \cite{T5}. However, in its construction, the authors did not take into account Bakushinsky's veto and the explicit dependence of such a dataset on the data error level $\delta$.
